prompt:
Create one continuous instrumental transformation between the supplied
opening and ending audio, using piano and vibraphone as shared musical
threads.

Retain a recognizable fragment of the opening's recurring piano figure.
Gradually reduce the eight-to-the-bar bass into fewer, longer notes.
Let the syncopated right-hand figures become more widely spaced and
less accented, with softer attacks and longer natural decay.

Allow the muted trumpet to recede. Keep occasional vibraphone tones
present, gradually softening their brightness and articulation.
Introduce a muted cello beneath the piano, sustaining a warm
middle-to-low register as the active bass pattern dissolves.

Move from an explicit swung pulse toward a spacious, loosely felt pulse.
Reduce note density before relaxing the rhythmic feel, avoiding an abrupt
switch from 120 BPM to 56 BPM. Approach the actual phrasing and harmony
of the ending audio reference.

Preserve harmonic continuity, an intimate room sound, and smooth
perceived loudness. Let the texture become warmer, more veiled, and
quieter through overlapping instrumental handovers. No alternating
sections, unrelated new theme, percussion fill, dramatic climax,
fade to silence, or final resolving chord.
